minor.issue: A URL path segment longer than the OS filename limit (NAME_MAX, ~255 bytes on ext4) causes `target.is_file()` inside arena_web.py:37 to raise OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long, which propagates as HTTP 500 (two tracebacks seen on /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log during T1's path-trick probe). The task explicitly asks for 'never a 500'. Fix suggestion (main agent): wrap the check in try/except OSError and fall through to the SPA/404 branch, e.g. `try: is_file = target.is_file(); rel = target.is_relative_to(ARENA_DIR) except OSError: is_file, rel = False, False` (or guard with `len(path.encode()) < 4000` before touching the filesystem). Short/normal long paths (<= NAME_MAX) already work correctly.

Known-not-a-bug list to NOT re-report: Cloudflare edge rewrites the hashed-asset Cache-Control to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' (origin headers are correct); the QA learner's real Matched paper page must not be Started; the arena_web.py 500 on a 5 000-byte URL is reported under backend_issues.minor and is a tiny guard the main agent can add.
rca_of_issue: arena_web 500 on an over-long URL: `Path.is_file()` on a target whose last segment exceeds NAME_MAX (255 bytes on ext4) calls `os.stat`, which raises OSError errno 36 before the file is checked. The exception bubbles up through FastAPI as an un-handled 500. Repro: curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:8001/api/arena/$(python3 -c "print('a'*5000)") → 500. Mitigation: wrap the stat / is_relative_to pair in a try/except OSError and treat it as 'no such file', or reject any URL whose decoded path.length() > NAME_MAX up front. Nothing here is a security issue: every traversal probe already lands on the SPA (same size as /api/arena) and never leaks a byte outside ARENA_DIR.
